recommended_tasks: Introduce a basic slot-booking mechanism (even a phone/WhatsApp register) so vendors commit to an arrival window, and start flagging peak-hour bunching so the problem is visible.

Deploy a digital appointment scheduler with defined slot windows.
 Mark and start enforcing a driver holding area away from the gate.
 Begin manually logging dock-in time.

Enforce system-generated slot windows with daily adherence tracking.
 Formalize and signpost the holding area.
 Start using dock-in time as the official SLA start-point for GRN TAT.
 Roll out QR/Booking-ID confirmations to the majority of vendors.

Automate vendor slot notifications and load-spread balancing across shift hours.
 Give the holding area real-time occupancy visibility.
 Make dock-in time system-captured with automated GRN-TAT breach alerts.
 Push QR/Booking-ID scanning above 90% of vendors with zero manual slot entries.

Introduce a single documentation checklist (vendor, invoice, indent qty) applied before unloading, even generic across vendor/courier.
 Start logging driver-ID and vehicle-number at the gate.

Split the checklist by vehicle type (vendor vs. courier).
 Check driver-ID/vehicle-number against the slot for a defined share of vehicles.
 Start temperature checks scoped specifically to 4°C SKUs (mushrooms etc.).

Introduce barcode/OCR-assisted matching to raise pre-unload verification coverage.
 Apply the >3°C-deviation temp-reject rule consistently for 4°C SKUs.
 Push driver-ID/vehicle authentication to the majority of vehicles.
 Log 100% of reefer vehicle temperatures.

Fully digitize gate verification end-to-end with an automated exception-flagging audit trail.
 Extend driver-ID/vehicle authentication and the temp-reject rule to over 90% of vehicles with zero exceptions.

Start rolling out biometric/facial-recognition coverage at main shift changeovers.
 Begin ad hoc zone-wise entry counts for at least the highest-risk zones (S&G, packing).

Extend facial-recognition coverage to the main changeover shifts.
 Define a warehouse-sizing-based headcount norm per zone and track actuals against it periodically.

Extend biometric coverage to all shifts and gates.
 Integrate zone-wise entry capture with the attendance system and reconcile daily against the sizing-based plan.

Push to 100% biometric plus physical-check coverage across all shifts/gates.
 Move zone-wise capture to real time with automated variance alerts against the sizing-based headcount plan.
Number the docks consistently and start using a manual dock-allocation sheet instead of ad hoc assignment.
Define dock allocation rules by vehicle size and start enforcing FIFO sequencing at the dock.

Move to system-based dock scheduling with size-matched allocation.
 Push FIFO adherence above 90% and guarantee green-channel vehicles unload within 15 minutes.
Automate dock-vehicle matching with real-time queuing to push utilization above 90%, FIFO adherence to 100%, and green-channel wait time under 10 minutes.

Fit buffers on at least a quarter of docks, prioritizing the highest-traffic ones.
 Start logging dock-damage incidents (even informally) as they happen.

Expand buffer coverage toward the halfway mark.
 Introduce a formal, if basic, penalty (warning/fine) for a driver's repeat dock-damage incident.
 Begin monthly physical dock-structure inspections logged separately from buffer damage.

Push buffer coverage into the 75-95% range.
 Formalize a graded penalty scale (warning to fine to vendor/transporter review) for repeat offenders.
 Move dock-structure inspection to weekly with defects tracked to closure.

Complete buffer coverage to 100%.
 Enforce the graded penalty scale strictly to hold repeat-offense rate under 2%.
 Run a preventive maintenance schedule and verify zero unresolved structural damage via weekly inspection.

Define a target unloading SLA (~500 units/person/hour for pre-packed material) and start marking a palletisation zone, even loosely.
 Introduce an informal pre-packed bypass flag for known vendors.

Assign dock-wise supervisor-led unloading teams.
 Enforce the crate-stacking SOP and keep the palletisation/S&G zones marked.
 Relocate waste disposal away from the inbound gate.
 Extend the bypass flag to 30-60% of eligible pre-packed loads.

Push supervisor-led teams to every shift.
 Mark FIFO lanes for S&G and a separate dry-category lane.
 Raise crate-stacking SOP compliance and bypass-flag usage into the 60-90% range.

Drive unloading SLA, crate-stacking, and bypass-flag compliance above 90% with zero space-constraint or cross-flow incidents.
 Fully integrate the bypass flag into the load-declaration/GRN step.

Start piloting digital weighment integration with the WMS/GRN system on a subset of lanes.
 Establish a minimum 1.5m clear aisle between weighment and staging.
 Put scale calibration on a defined (even if not daily) schedule.

Extend digital weighment integration to 30-60% of transactions.
 Begin shifting weighment to the unloading stage (ahead of S&G) for some vendor categories to cut PO-closure delay.

Push digital weighment coverage to 60-90%.
 Make weighment-at-unloading-stage the default for the majority of vendors.
 Move scale recalibration to daily with tare memory per packaging type.
 Retain digital weight logs as an audit trail.

Complete digital weighment integration above 90% with zero manual entry.
 Make same-day PO closure the norm.
 Use the digital weight log routinely for supplier invoice reconciliation and shrinkage analysis.

Introduce an informal capacity check (even a phone call to the dock supervisor) before releasing any vehicle.
 Designate (even if unenforced) a waiting/parking zone for held vehicles.
 Start issuing an exit slip on gate-out.

Define a formal capacity check with a stated time window (e.g., 15 minutes for dock bay plus staging space) and route 'no' decisions to the holding area.
 Introduce a basic reject-vs-hold rule.
 Make exit-slip issuance standard.

Extend capacity-gated release to the majority of gate-ins.
 Formalize the full reject/temp-reject/hold/bypass decision taxonomy.
 Add outbound-seal verification to gate-out.
 Install physical enablers (multi-lane entry, boom barrier, CCTV/tablet).

Push capacity-gated release above 90% in real time, tied live to the dock-management and staging systems.
 Apply the full decision taxonomy with a complete audit trail.
 Make gate-out fully controlled (exit slip plus seal verification on 100% of dispatches).
 Add a weighbridge where applicable.
Start measuring Dock-to-Stock Time end-to-end (even as a simple manual timestamp difference) so the current 8+ hour baseline becomes visible.
Track Dock-to-Stock Time daily as a standing facility KPI, not just a monthly average.
Break Dock-to-Stock Time into its three stages (dock-in, GRN TAT, putaway TAT) to identify and act on the single slowest stage.
Automate real-time, end-to-end tracking with stage-wise breach alerts so Dock-to-Stock Time is actively managed, not just reported.
Start timing unloading per vehicle (dock-in to unload-complete), even manually, to establish a baseline against the 90-minute mark.
Track Unloading TAT per vehicle (not just in aggregate) for the majority of dock-ins.
Review Unloading TAT daily against the unloading SLA and act on outliers.
Move to real-time per-vehicle tracking feeding directly into the Dock-to-Stock Time KPI, driving TAT under 25 minutes.
Start timing Putaway TAT (GRN-complete to putaway-complete), even as a manual daily average.
Track Putaway TAT daily by zone to see where goods are getting stuck between GRN and shelf.
Add SKU-level tracking and set a defined target TAT per zone/SKU, reviewing actuals against it.
Move to real-time zone/SKU tracking so Putaway TAT closes the loop into the Dock-to-Stock Time KPI, driving it under 1 hour.
Document at least 3-4 of the 9 core QMS elements, starting with policy, SOPs, and a responsibility matrix.
Complete documentation for 5-6 elements and put them into active use, with at least an annual review cycle.
Extend to 7-8 elements with quarterly review and clear ownership assigned to each.
Complete all 9 elements, version-control them, and link them to a closed-loop CAPA process with under 5-day average closure time.

Define a sampling percentage and a written AQR format, even if not yet consistently applied.
 Require quality-team sign-off before GRN posting (even if it currently happens late).

Fix sampling at ~10% with a 20% defect-rejection threshold.
 Make GRN approval procedurally dependent on quality clearance (even if still manual/paper-based).
 Apply the AQR before unloading for the majority of lots.

Segment sampling/rejection by category (FnV vs. dry) with batch/expiry and shelf-life checks.
 Make GRN posting a hard system hold pending quality clearance.
 Start tracking QC/vehicle rejection by vendor and SKU into a periodic supplier scorecard.

Digitize sampling/rejection norms per SKU category with under 2% inspection error.
 Make GRN release fully system-enforced with zero exceptions and a full sign-off audit trail.
 Run the AQR and supplier scorecard in real time, feeding vendor reviews.
Define a basic RTV process, even informal, to move same-day closure above 30%.
Formalize the RTV policy by SKU category (hard/soft goods) to push same-day closure into the 50-75% range.
Track RTV performance and review pending-returns space usage weekly to push same-day closure into the 75-95% range.
Fully systemize RTV to sustain over 95% same-day closure with zero aged-return inventory beyond 24 hours.
Start tracking complaint rate consistently (both as % of volume and in PPM), even without root-cause analysis yet.
Categorize complaints monthly and benchmark PPM against the industry band.

Add root-cause analysis with a 7-day corrective-action closure target.
 Track PPM weekly against a defined benchmark.
Move to real-time tracking with 48-hour closed-loop resolution, holding complaint rate under 1% and PPM under 50.
Start logging every near-miss and safety incident, not just reportable injuries, to get a real weekly count.
Review the logged incidents monthly and begin categorizing root causes, even without corrective-action tracking yet.
Move incident review to daily and track corrective actions through to closure for the majority of incidents.
Hold incidents to zero reportable and under 1 near-miss/month, with corrective actions closed within a defined SLA and results feeding the QMS risk-analysis element.
Start manual spot-checks of chiller/freezer temperatures a few times a day, even without formal logging yet.
Log daily manual readings for the main cold zones to push compliance into the 85-95% range.
Install continuous sensor monitoring for the majority of cold-chain zones with daily breach review.
Extend sensor monitoring to 100% of cold-chain zones with real-time breach alerts, holding compliance above 98%.
Run a 5S pilot in one area and start basic floor demarcation there (aisles, storage) to lift the audit score above 40%.

Extend Sort/Set/Shine facility-wide with quarterly audits.
 Expand demarcation to include S&G/packing space and storage marking.

Standardize 5S across all zones with monthly audits and biannual training.
 Extend demarcation to buffer-pallet staging and packaging-material storage.

Sustain 5S with daily checks and a documented Kaizen count.
 Complete 100% zone demarcation (including tools/machinery) with colour-coding, auditing demarcation adherence as part of the daily check.
Deploy a second lean principle (e.g., start value-stream mapping) and introduce PDCA on at least a few processes.

Deploy a third principle and embed PDCA in 20-50% of processes.
 Start tracking 2-3 of the 8 waste types.

Add pull/JIT replenishment as a fourth principle.
 Push PDCA to 50-80% of processes and track 5-6 waste types with quarterly reduction targets.

Fully embed all 5 lean principles with PDCA in over 80% of processes.
 Track all 8 waste types with measurable year-on-year reduction above 10%.
Document standard ITL flows for the highest-volume scenarios to push documentation above 30%.
Document the major exception scenarios alongside standard flows to reach 50-75% coverage.
Version-control the documentation and review it twice a year, pushing coverage into the 75-95% range.
Digitize and review documentation quarterly, closing any undocumented recurring exception to reach over 95% coverage.
Define size/quality standards and a throughput SLA (~70 units/person/hour) for the first 30% of SKUs/stations, even if compliance is uneven.

Extend standards and throughput-SLA tracking to 30-60% of SKUs/stations.
 Start assigning experienced manpower to piece-category SKUs, even if inconsistently.

Extend to 60-90% of SKUs/stations with monthly grading-accuracy audits above 90%.
 Make experienced-manpower assignment for piece-category SKUs consistent.
Complete standards and SLA tracking for 100% of SKUs/stations with weekly audits above 95% accuracy and a corrective feedback loop.
Define packaging material by SKU for the first half of SKUs and start tracking a shift-level SLA on a subset of lines.

Define packaging material for all SKUs.
 Introduce a formed-box staging shelf and begin aligning some vendors to FC pack standards to remove re-packing.

Push productivity toward the 100-120 units/person/hour band with daily gang-output tracking.
 Extend FC-standard vendor alignment and dedicated chilled packing to 60-90% of applicable lines/shifts.

Sustain productivity above 120 units/person/hour.
 Eliminate the re-pack sub-process for over 90% of applicable vendors and route 100% of chilled SKUs through a dedicated chilled station, tracked and improved monthly.
Set the 4-person-per-table norm and start applying an S&G-to-packing table ratio, even if compliance is under 40%.

Push table-norm and ratio compliance into the 40-70% range.
 Begin an inter-vendor cleaning step, even if inconsistent.

Monitor table norm and ratio adherence via regular floor walks to reach 70-95%.
 Make inter-vendor cleaning standard practice.

Maintain over 95% adherence with real-time floor supervision.
 Enforce inter-vendor cleaning with zero cross-contamination incidents.
Start tracking shrinkage in aggregate (even without category splits) to establish a baseline against the 5% ceiling.

Split shrinkage tracking by SKU category against benchmark ranges.
 Start tracking seasonal RTV loss by season.

Push category-level shrinkage within benchmark for over 80% of categories.
 Review the seasonal-loss trend monthly with corrective action for outliers.
Hold shrinkage at or below benchmark for all categories and seasonal loss at 1.5% or below even in monsoon, with monthly root-cause review and documented reduction actions.
Start measuring the repack/re-stickering rate consistently, even without a target yet, to get past pure anecdote.
Set a 5% target and begin cause-coding rework into its specific drivers (banana re-sort, late ripeness segregation, idle organic-table time).
Act on the cause-coded drivers - stop banana re-sorting, move ripeness segregation to the S&G stage, convert the organic table to multi-use - tracking weekly to bring the rate into the 2-5% range.
Sustain elimination of all three root causes for 2+ consecutive quarters, tracking daily, to hold the repack rate under 2%.
Start tracking packing accuracy (correct SKU, quantity, and label per unit/case) distinctly from piece-level output checks, even in aggregate, to establish a baseline above 96%.
Track it per packer/shift for the majority of lines.
Review per-packer/shift accuracy daily and correct recurring error patterns to push into the 98-99% band.
Move to real-time per-packer/shift tracking to sustain accuracy above 99%.
Add a second forecasting layer (e.g., seasonal on top of baseline) to lift forecast accuracy above 60%.

Add a third layer (event-based) and start tracking time-of-day demand curves for at least half of SKUs/stores.
 Give new stores a defined generic ramp-up curve instead of guesswork.

Add the fourth layer (typically time-of-day or hyperlocal) and extend it to 70-90% of stores.
 Root-cause SKU-level forecast error monthly.
 Bridge new-store gaps with a comparable-store proxy model.

Activate and continuously calibrate all 5 layers against actuals.
 Automate recalibration for hourly volatility and SKU-level accuracy.
 Cut the new-store proxy-to-actual transition to 2-4 weeks.
Define a second inventory-planning component (e.g., a seasonal buffer) beyond regular+buffer stock.
Add a third component (e.g., SKU assortment) and enforce FEFO for the majority of fresh SKUs to bring stockout/excess incidents into the 5-10% band.
Add the fourth component (seasonal and festive buffers both applied) and move batch/expiry visibility to near-real-time to isolate the stockout-vs-waste trade-off.
Automate all 5 components with weekly review and real-time, system-enforced batch/expiry visibility to hold incidents under 2% of SKUs monthly.

Define the replenishment formula (Forecast Demand + Safety Stock - Current Inventory) and run it at least once a day.
 Introduce a basic reorder-point trigger for a subset of SKUs.

Run replenishment daily on the standard formula.
 Extend the reorder-point trigger to 30-60% of SKUs with a manually-invoked emergency top-up process.
 Start tracking DoI by category.

Move to twice-daily replenishment with a defined wave split and lead-time/buffer-capacity factored in.
 Extend reorder-point coverage to 60-90% of SKUs with an SLA-bound emergency top-up.
 Track DoI by SKU against a target band.

Fully automate the twice-daily-plus cycle with an optimized wave split and lead-time-adjusted safety stock.
 Extend reorder-point/ARS coverage above 90%.
 Eliminate replenishment-receipt dock congestion and storage overflow via slotted receiving.
Extend defined manpower planning to a third role and start tracking (even without acting on) attrition.

Cover a fourth role.
 Introduce a surge-planning trigger and a gig-flex ratio for at least some shifts, even if reactive.

Cover a fifth role with shift-level granularity.
 Build shift design around the full diurnal demand curve and put an active attrition/gig-supply mitigation plan in place.

Cover all 6 roles with daily granularity and pre-built capacity buffers.
 Make surge planning and gig-flex proactive on over 90% of shifts, with attrition and gig-supply risk mitigated via a pre-qualified backup pool.

Move to at least 1 planned warehouse-to-dark-store cycle per day (from ad hoc dispatch).
 Start applying route/truck-load optimization to at least some routes.

Run 1-2 cycles per day with a defined (e.g., 70/30) wave split.
 Extend route/truck-load optimization to 30-60% of routes.
 Check freezer/cold-chain capacity before dispatch for temperature-sensitive SKUs.

Push to 2 cycles per day with 70-90% wave-split adherence.
 Extend route optimization to 60-90% of routes.
 Give pre-live dark stores a defined, separate inward SOP.

Run 2+ cycles per day with wave-split adherence above 90%, dynamically adjusted to dark-store stock in real time.
 Extend route optimization above 90% with OPH at/above target.
 Plan freezer capacity dynamically with zero breaches.
Define and start using a D-minus planning day, even inconsistently, to push fill rate above 70%.
Formalize the D-minus planning day for FnV/dry categories to push fill rate into the 80-90% range.
Follow the D-minus cycle consistently and root-cause variance monthly to push fill rate into the 90-95% range.
Follow D-minus planning on 100% of days, holding over/under-planning variance under 5% and fill rate above 95%.
Start tracking at least one supplier dimension (OTIF or price) in aggregate.
Track 2-3 dimensions by vendor on a periodic (e.g., quarterly) cadence, even without linking to sourcing decisions yet.

Track all four dimensions by vendor monthly, feeding a basic scorecard.
 Start adjusting sourcing allocation for chronic underperformers and defining contracting/hedging for key SKUs.

Move to real-time, vendor-and-SKU-level tracking via an automated scorecard driving sourcing/tiering decisions.
 Hold OTIF above 95% and hedge/contract price volatility for the majority of high-value categories.
Start reconciling Indent against actual inward/dispatch, even just in aggregate, to establish a variance baseline.
Reconcile daily for the majority of SKUs/stores to push variance into the 10-20% band.
Root-cause the variance monthly to push it into the 5-10% band.
Move to real-time reconciliation, reporting indent accuracy as a standing KPI alongside forecast accuracy, holding variance under 5%.
Start enforcing FIFO picking/putaway in at least the highest-turnover zones.
Extend enforcement to the majority of zones, even without system validation yet.
Add system guidance for FIFO at putaway and picking across most zones.
Make FIFO system-enforced with automatic exception flagging to sustain compliance above 95%.
Start a periodic (even ad hoc) cycle-count process to establish an accuracy baseline above 90%.
Put cycle counts on a defined periodic schedule to push accuracy into the 95-98% range.
Move to weekly cycle counts with variance root-caused to push accuracy into the 98-99.5% range.
Move to continuous/perpetual cycle counting with real-time variance alerts to sustain accuracy above 99.5%.
Start tracking expiry loss as a distinct value/sales ratio, even without linking it to FEFO yet.
Track it monthly and begin linking it conceptually to FEFO compliance.
Review it monthly against FEFO compliance to close the loop and push loss into the 0.5-1% band.
Track it in real time, directly reconciled against FEFO/FIFO compliance, to hold loss under 0.5%.

Push throughput into the 75-90%-of-benchmark band via targeted layout or process changes.

 Close out lessons-learned post-project to sustain over 90% on-time, in-budget delivery.

Track monthly or more frequently, documenting a continuous downward trend below budget.

Start tracking short-pick % distinctly to establish a baseline below 10%.
